title: Science Collaboration Centre (formerly Business Hub), Chalk River Laboratories
jurisdiction: Chalk River, Ontario; federal site administered by Canadian Nuclear Laboratories
code_edition: 2015 National Building Code of Canada and 2015 National Fire Code; the report says there was no formal municipal permitting process

facts.text: The CNL case study describes a six-storey Science Collaboration Centre with CLT floors, walls and roof on Levels 2-6 and glulam framing.
The report says the federal site used national codes and third-party reviews rather than a formal municipal permitting process.

It describes an NBC height issue caused by a sloping site and measuring building height from the lowest ground elevation; the alternative design described used concrete for the first two levels and timber above.
The report also describes increased sprinkler density by one hazard classification and fire-department access at Level 2 as measures discussed for the building-height issue.
The report cites a 2019 supplier Code Compliance Report, document B703-20000-REPT-001, but does not include it.

limitations: The case study covers three separate CNL buildings; this candidate isolates the Science Collaboration Centre issue and shares the same original report with the Support Facility candidate.
The cited Business Hub Code Compliance Report B703-20000-REPT-001 (Morrison Hershfield, 2019) was not located as a public attachment.
The report is not the full alternative-solution submission or final approval file.
